task_brief: Day 2 of "Advanced Studio Technique and Materials" (unit 1, grade 10) is a first concept model on two-dimensional media in depth. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Produce a technically ambitious studio work with a documented technique study and a safety plan. Today's work contributes to that by handling two-dimensional media in depth at the concept model a stage, against the unit's wider topics of sustained technique development, two-dimensional media in depth, three-dimensional and sculptural methods, and printmaking or mixed media. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study the first model work for two-dimensional media in depth closely before making anything of your own. Write what you notice in three passes: first what is literally there, then how it is put together, then what effect that has on a viewer or listener. Name the specific choice the maker used to create two-dimensional media in depth. Then reproduce that one element — not the whole work — in your own short study, and write one sentence on what was harder than it looked. Use only public-domain, openly licensed, or supplied model works, and cite whatever you studied. Use the attached Academy-original Model A as the first model work; no outside search or teacher-supplied example is required. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about two-dimensional media in depth, and it belongs to "Advanced Studio Technique and Materials", which also covers separate topics such as sustained technique development. Close out with this check before you stop: Explain the modelled approach to two-dimensional media in depth in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong. At grade 10 the bar is independent work that justifies its approach against a named alternative you considered and rejected, with the trade-off stated concretely.

sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g10-arts-and-music-u01-l02

Lesson focus: two-dimensional media in depth

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL A — "Near, Middle, Far." Imagine a small dark circle at upper left, a medium striped rectangle at centre, and a large pale triangle touching the lower edge. A thin curved line links them. The strongest contrast surrounds the circle. Intent: guide the eye from circle to rectangle to triangle. Notice placement, contrast, repetition, and scale. For a one-element pencil study, draw three shapes and alter exactly one choice. Use it to study two-dimensional media in depth; describe evidence before judging and adapt the example rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-original Model A as the first model work; no outside search or teacher-supplied example is required.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: Observation is recorded in three distinct passes: literal content, construction, and effect.
The specific maker's choice that creates two-dimensional media in depth is named, not described in general praise.
One element — not the whole work — is reproduced as a short study, with a note on what proved harder than expected.
Every studied work is public domain, openly licensed, or supplied for this task, and is cited.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting two-dimensional media in depth.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for two-dimensional media in depth follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for two-dimensional media in depth, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to two-dimensional media in depth works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of two-dimensional media in depth, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking two-dimensional media in depth mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply two-dimensional media in depth under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on two-dimensional media in depth rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
